source: LANGUAGE_LEXICON.md section 2, 29 topic groups; NOT ACT authored dialogue corpus
rules: Every backticked expression in the 29 source groups is retained, including multiword chunks. This is not a list of approved lemmas or a translation dictionary.
role productive/receptive is a source catalogue recommendation and not automatic proof of M-level necessity or learning.
Identical surface strings in different groups retain all occurrences; disambiguation, declension, inflection, noun gender and sense ID are separate editorial tasks.
Groups and horizons are independent of story days, NPC biographies, plot vocabulary and ACT scene statistics.
Full F1 is the approved act inventory, not equal to all entries in this exploratory catalogue; all approved entries are available from start.
Meaningful usage frequency is not derived from count of catalogue occurrences.
In 73 independent language A/B examples, 36 additional surface tokens were reviewed: 27 form aliases, 2 placeholder names, 7 extra lexical candidates. None came from story content.

After qualitative goal-alignment fixes, the A/B examples were re-tokenized. Observed form counts always derive from the current 73-unit canonical examples; extra candidates are tracked separately, never counted as observed.
After removing duplicated language examples, re-evaluated 80 pairs and added candidate normalization for hast, willst, liest, spielt, gezeigt.
Every 463 independent catalogue expression now has at least one candidate Russian meaning; polysemy, word sense granularity, flexion, and reverse lookup remain editorial work and not proven F1.

Synchronized new independent lexical entries (including wohin, sehen, 0–12 numerals, location, emotion, and polite Herr) to LANGUAGE_LEXICON.md; no mandatory practice load assigned by simple catalogue inclusion.
All 34 grammar-example contrasts now checked for lexical bases: ein/der/die/ohne/bei/liegen/als plus candidate morphologies for forms such as dich/ihn/den/liegt.

rules: All entries/queries are derived from independent M/G/LO and not from narrative-specific dialogue.
A search query may return multiple dictionary senses; grammatical role, context and register are required for disambiguation.
A Russian reverse search lists neutral candidate words and grammar notes, never completes the present task automatically.
A lookup hit is not evidence of acquisition. Unknown, misspelled or ambiguous queries have explicit no-match/uncertain states.
Capitalized Sie at sentence start is ambiguous without verb/person/context; do not determine register from capital alone.
The complete approved act vocabulary will be available on F1 from beginning, irrespective of language horizon.

validation.unknown_query: return uncertainty and candidates rather than invented single translation
